THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Split Plate Chili Hot Dogs

One chili base. Six beef dogs. Two adult plates + two kid plates. Split at the bun (keto vs regular) + toppings (red onion + banana peppers vs optional mustard) + presentation (composed vs deconstructed). 510 cal / 58g protein adult. 45 min end-to-end.

YIELD4 servings
TOTAL TIME45 min
COOK METHODAir fryer
EST. / SERVING~510 cal | ~58g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: REDUCE THE CHILI UNTIL VISIBLE LIQUID IS GONE. This is the entire cling step. A wet chili soaks the bun and slides off the dog. Uncover, medium heat, stir occasionally, taste for salt only AFTER reducing.

Ingredients

PROTEIN

  • 6 beef hot dogs (Nathan's / Ball Park Angus / Kirkland uncured — pick one)

MELT

  • 3 slices Velveeta Original (1/2 slice per dog)

ADULT TOPPINGS

  • Finely chopped red onion, to taste
  • Sliced banana peppers, to taste

COMPONENT (12-serving base, this dinner uses 6)

  • 1 batch Hot Dog Chili Base (2 lb 93/7 ground beef + Spiceology BBQ rub or alternative seasoning + Dijon + Worcestershire + tomato paste + bone broth)

ADULT BUNS

  • 3 Nature's Own Keto Hot Dog Buns (1.5 per adult plate)

Option 1

  • 2 Ball Park regular hot dog buns (1 per kid)
  • Yellow mustard, to taste (optional — only if they ask)

Allergens: gluten, dairy, mustard, fish. Possible soy

AT THE PLATE — same chili base, same beef dogs, same Velveeta. Adult vs kid forks on bun (Nature's Own keto vs Ball Park regular) + toppings (red onion + banana peppers vs optional mustard) + presentation (composed vs deconstructed).

Method

Shared base

  1. 1.CHILI BASE. Make the Hot Dog Chili Base (or reheat 6 stored servings). Brown 2 lb 93/7 ground beef, season with 3 tbsp Spiceology BBQ rub (or the alternative blend), stir in Dijon + Worcestershire, add tomato paste + bone broth, reduce uncovered until the visible liquid is gone. Divide into 12 servings; use 6 tonight.
  2. 2.SCORE THE DOGS. Shallow diagonal cuts on 6 beef dogs — 3-4 marks per dog, no more than 1/4 through. Char surface without splitting.
  3. 3.AIR FRY. 400°F for ~7 min. Check early — air fryers vary. Pull when the scores have opened and the edges are lightly charred.
  4. 4.WARM BOTH BUN STACKS. 3 Nature's Own keto (adult) + 2 Ball Park regular (kid). 30 sec at 300°F in the air fryer after the dogs come out. Cold buns crack; warm buns cradle the dog.
  5. 5.1/2 VELVEETA SLICE PER BUN. 6 buns × 1/2 slice = 3 slices total. Fold the slice INTO the bun before the dog — the hot chili melts it in seconds.

Adult — 1.5 Loaded Chili Dogs on Keto Buns + Red Onion + Banana Peppers

  1. 6.ADULT TOPPINGS PREP. Finely chop red onion. Slice banana peppers (or use pre-jarred). Both stay raw — no cook time.
  2. 7.ASSEMBLE. 3 Nature's Own keto buns → 1/2 Velveeta slice each → hot dog → 1 serving chili spooned over each dog.
  3. 8.FINISH. Scatter red onion + banana peppers over the adult chili dogs. Plate 1.5 dogs per adult (~510 cal / 58g protein).

Kid — Deconstructed Chili Dog Tray · Option 1

  1. 6.KID TRAY. Divided tray. 1 Ball Park regular bun (opened flat, 1/2 Velveeta slice folded inside) in one compartment.
  2. 7.CHILI WELL. 1 serving hot chili into a small well or ramekin on the tray. Kids can dip or spoon.
  3. 8.DOGS. 1 whole beef dog in the bun compartment (for building). 0.5 beef dog sliced into rounds on the side (for snacking).
  4. 9.OPTIONAL MUSTARD. Only if they ask. Small squeeze on the tray or on the bun.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult — 1.5 Loaded Chili Dogs on Keto Buns + Red Onion + Banana Peppers: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid — Deconstructed Chili Dog Tray: Serve the kid portion as described above.

Keys to success

  • SCORE, DON'T SLICE. Shallow diagonal cuts along each dog — 3-4 marks per dog, no more than 1/4 through. The cuts open in the air fryer and create char surface without splitting the dog in half.
  • TWO BUN STACKS, WARM SEPARATELY. Nature's Own keto for adults + Ball Park regular for kids. Both warm briefly (30 sec at 300°F in the air fryer after the dogs come out) — cold buns kill the plate.

If something fails

Chili is soupy / running off the dog: Didn't reduce enough. Uncover, medium-high heat, stir until the visible liquid is gone. Taste; add salt only AFTER reducing (concentration changes the salt read).

Buns cracked / cold: Cold buns crack. Air-fry both bun stacks 30 sec at 300°F right after the dogs come out. Or microwave in a clean towel 15 sec.

Kid won't touch the chili dog: That's what the deconstructed tray is for. Leave chili in a well, 1 dog + 0.5 on the side, bun folded. They pick up the dog plain if that's what they want tonight. Most kids come back for the chili on day 2.

Adult plate flat / one-note: Skipped the red onion + banana peppers. Both are 30-second adds. Onion sharpness + banana pepper acid is the difference between 'hot dog' and 'loaded chili dog.'

Dogs split too much in the air fryer: Scored too deep. Shallow diagonal cuts — 3-4 marks per dog, no more than 1/4 through. Don't cut like a filet.

Chili tastes flat: Underseasoned. If you used the alternative blend (paprika + garlic + onion + salt), taste after reducing and add more salt or a pinch of smoked paprika. Or dial up 1 tsp Worcestershire for umami depth.

Ran out of chili for the dinner: The base makes 12 servings; this dinner uses 6. If you're short, portion 1 serving per dog and skip the drizzle. Or add a splash of broth to loosen a smaller amount and stretch it.

Storage and reheating

Store: Cool cooked chili promptly and refrigerate in shallow airtight containers within 2 hours. Cooked hot dogs 3-4 days fridge. Assemble plates fresh — chili + buns don't hold well pre-assembled.

Reheat: Chili: covered saucepan on medium 3-5 min, stir occasionally. Reheat to 165°F. Hot dogs: air fryer 3 min at 350°F to re-char. Buns fresh — never reheat a chili dog assembled.

Lasts: Chili base: 3-4 days fridge, 3-4 months freezer for best quality (per USDA leftovers guidance). Assembled chili dogs are a same-night dinner.

Make this when

You want chili dog night without cooking two separate dinners. One 12-serving chili base = 4 plates tonight + 6 servings reserved for chili mac or another comfort build later in the week. Adults get loaded on keto buns; kids build their own on a divided tray. No-bean chili — thick enough to stay on the bun.

Brands I use

Nature's Own
Keto Hot Dog Buns (~50 cal / 5g protein per bun)
Tier 3 adult carb. The macro unlock for chili dog night. Regular hot dog buns run ~130 cal / 4g protein — Nature's Own keto cuts calories in half AND adds a bit of protein while still eating like a real bun. Skip these and the 510 cal / 58g protein adult target dies.
Ball Park
Regular Hot Dog Buns (~130 cal / 4g protein per bun)
Tier 3 kid carb. Kids get NORMAL bread — soft, familiar, non-diet-y. The macro-hack is not for them. Sub any regular hot dog bun.
Velveeta
Original Slices (~70 cal / 4g protein per slice; use 1/2 slice per dog)
Tier 2 melt. Half a slice melts under the hot chili in seconds — no separate cheese step, no shred, no oiliness. Sub American slices for a shorter ingredient list.
Spiceology
Beef-Infused BBQ Rub (chili seasoning)
The seasoning that carries the chili base. Smoky, beef-forward, no filler. If unavailable, the base recipe documents a 2 tsp paprika + 2 tsp garlic powder + 2 tsp onion powder + 2 tsp salt alternative — it replaces the rub, not on top.
Hot Dog Chili Base
Cookbook cross-link — the reusable component
This dinner is anchored by the 12-serving Hot Dog Chili Base. Full method + macros on the cookbook page. Uses 6 servings tonight; the other 6 chain into chili mac, baked potatoes, fries, bowls, or another chili dog dinner.
